editorial:
Imagine waking up in a world that feels like a weird dream where nothing is quite what it seems. You follow a college professor and his strange friend who travels from place to place. These two get caught up in messy love triangles and run into people who seem to be playing a game with life and death. The whole movie has a very odd, floaty feeling to it, and the colors are bright and bold. It does not follow a straight line like most stories do, but instead, it drags you into a strange mood that feels both fancy and creepy at the same time.

What really pops are the visuals and the way the actors move, which makes everything feel like a stage play. Some parts might feel a bit slow or confusing if you want a clear plot, but that is part of the fun. If you like movies that make you think and feel uneasy, you will love this one. Since it is so visually striking, you should definitely try to find the 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection to see every detail. If you are in a rush, renting it on Apple TV is a great way to check it out first.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up with a strange sense of fate and death. You see the characters caught in a cycle where life and death blend together. The professor and his friend face their ends in ways that feel more like a performance than a tragedy. It ends by showing that these people were never really in control, and their lives were just a series of odd events leading to an inevitable, quiet stop.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves weird stories and beautiful art styles.
